goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38 — New OR branch deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount>1 regardless of method (EMAIL/WHATSAPP) or scheduled state, widening delete scope beyond SMS.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — prisma.update inside catch is unguarded; if it throws (e.g. row deleted by concurrent run/cancellation, P2025) the error escapes the loop and aborts all remaining reminders.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` in the `catch` block (and also in the `else` branch) without any nested try/catch. If that update throws (e.g., Prisma P2025 because the reminder row was deleted/cancelled or removed by another concurrent run), the exception will escape the `catch` and abort processing of subsequent reminders in the loop. This failure mode is introduced/exposed by the new retryCount update logic shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:189 — Catch also fires when Twilio scheduling succeeded but the scheduled:true update failed, so retry re-schedules a duplicate SMS and eventual delete orphans the live Twilio message (referenceId lost, cannot cancel).

adjudication.rationale: In the new logic, any error inside the `try` (including a failure of the post-Twilio `prisma.workflowReminder.update` that sets `scheduled: true` / `referenceId`) will be caught by the `catch`, which now increments `retryCount` but does not persist the Twilio `sid`. That leaves the reminder appearing unscheduled for the next run, causing a re-schedule and potential duplicate SMS. The later `deleteMany` now also deletes records with `retryCount > 1`, which can remove the DB row while an already-scheduled Twilio message exists (orphaning it). This failure mode is consistent with the diff’s added retry/delete behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — Retry increment uses stale read value (retryCount + 1) instead of atomic {increment: 1}, so overlapping cron runs lose increments and both may send/schedule the same SMS.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:158 — Reminders with empty message or missing sendTo (and those skipped at line 68) never increment retryCount, so they bypass the retry cap and are silently retried every run forever.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows retryCount added, selected, and incremented only in the Twilio-schedule failure path (the new `else` after `if (scheduledSMS)` and in the `catch`). It does not show any logic for “empty message”, “missing sendTo”, or a “skip at line 68”, so the claim that those skipped reminders never increment retryCount cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38 — Reminders exceeding the retry limit are hard-deleted silently with no log, alert, or user-visible failure state, so dropped SMS reminders are undetectable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `retryCount` field and then hard-deletes reminders via `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { OR: [...] { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] } })` with no logging or status update. This does mean reminders that exceed the retry threshold are removed with no explicit trace in this handler. However, the diff doesn’t establish that a persistent failure state or logging is required for correctness; it’s more an observability/product concern than a verifiable functional defect from the change alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — The await prisma.update inside catch is unguarded, so if it throws (e.g. the reminder was deleted or the DB is down) the whole loop aborts and the handler never responds.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `await prisma.workflowReminder.update({ ... retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 })` inside the `catch (error)` block (and also in the `else` branch). That update is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If it throws (e.g., DB unavailable, record missing), the exception will propagate out of the loop/handler and can prevent the API handler from completing and responding, whereas previously the catch only logged.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — If the scheduled:true update fails after Twilio has already scheduled the SMS, catch bumps retryCount and the reminder stays unscheduled, so the next run schedules a duplicate SMS.

adjudication.rationale: In the try block, the code schedules the SMS and then marks the reminder as scheduled via `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { scheduled: true, referenceId: ... } })`. If that DB update throws, the `catch` now updates only `retryCount` (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) and does not set `scheduled: true` or persist the Twilio `sid`. That leaves the reminder eligible to be picked up again (it’s still “unscheduled”) on the next run, which can cause the SMS to be scheduled again (duplicate) despite the first Twilio schedule having succeeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — retryCount is written as a stale in-memory value + 1 rather than an atomic { increment: 1 }, so overlapping cron runs lose increments.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39 — The boundary gt: 1 deletes a reminder after only 2 failed attempts (one retry), which is likely off by one from the intended retry limit and is an undocumented magic number.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a cleanup condition `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` (scheduleSMSReminders.ts). Since `retryCount` is incremented on failure (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`), reminders will be deleted once `retryCount` reaches 2, meaning at most 2 scheduling attempts (initial + 1 retry) before they’re removed on a subsequent run. Whether this is an off-by-one “bug” depends on intended retry policy, which isn’t shown in the diff, but the `gt: 1` threshold is a hard-coded/magic number with potentially surprising behavior and no in-code explanation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:158 — Reminders with an empty message or no sendTo never get retryCount incremented, so they are re-processed on every run until scheduledDate passes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows retryCount being incremented when SMS scheduling fails inside the try block’s new `else` branch (when `scheduledSMS` is falsy) and inside the `catch`. It does not show any branch that skips processing due to an empty message or missing `sendTo`, so the claim that such reminders "never get retryCount incremented" cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39 — New deleteMany OR branch `retryCount > 1` is not scoped to method SMS, so any EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminder with retryCount>1 is hard-deleted by the SMS cron.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` filter was changed to `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`. The second OR branch has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint, so any `WorkflowReminder` of any method (e.g., EMAIL/WHATSAPP) with `retryCount > 1` will be deleted by this SMS scheduling endpoint/cron, causing unintended cross-method data deletion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39 — Failed reminders are permanently hard-deleted after retries with no audit trail or soft-delete, losing reminder records silently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` and increments it on scheduling failures, then `deleteMany` now hard-deletes any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1` (regardless of method/date) via the new `OR` clause. This does permanently remove failed reminder records without any soft-delete/audit field being added in the diff, so the concern about losing records is grounded, though whether this is an actual defect vs. intended cleanup isn’t verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/schema.prisma:1000 — No index covers the new `retryCount` delete predicate, and inside the OR it forces a full sequential scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron run.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new deleteMany predicate `OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` and introduces the `retryCount` column in Prisma schema/migration, but does not add any corresponding index in `schema.prisma` (only existing indexes on `bookingUid` and `workflowStepId` remain). This is a concrete, diff-grounded potential performance issue for the cron cleanup query, though the claim that it *must* “force a full sequential scan” is query-planner dependent and not strictly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20240508134359_add_retry_count_to_workflow_reminder/migration.sql:2 — Migration ships no down/rollback script; ADD COLUMN NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 is safe (metadata-only on PG11+) but reverting requires a manual DROP COLUMN.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a Prisma SQL migration that only contains an `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT 0;` statement. Prisma migrations typically don’t include a separate down/rollback script in the migration file, so flagging “ships no down/rollback script” isn’t a verifiable defect or actionable review issue from this diff alone (and the PG11+ metadata-only claim/rollback requirements aren’t established by the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38 — The retryCount>1 OR branch has no SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes EMAIL/WhatsApp reminders too.

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts, the deleteMany where-clause was changed to `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`. The second OR branch has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so it will delete any WorkflowReminder rows (including non-SMS methods like EMAIL/WhatsApp, if present) once `retryCount > 1`, causing unintended cross-method data deletion from the SMS cron.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — The retryCount update in the catch block is unguarded; if it throws (e.g. P2025 or DB error), the whole cron loop aborts and the remaining reminders never get processed or answered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` inside the `catch (error)` block (and also in an `else` branch). If that update throws (e.g., record missing/P2025, transient DB error), there is no nested try/catch around it, so the exception will escape the catch block and abort the handler’s loop, preventing remaining reminders from being processed and potentially preventing a response from being sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:169 — If the DB update fails after Twilio has scheduled the SMS, the catch counts a retry and the next run schedules a duplicate SMS.

adjudication.rationale: The `try` covers both the Twilio scheduling call and the subsequent Prisma `update` that writes `referenceId` (and other fields). If Twilio successfully schedules an SMS but the Prisma update throws, execution goes to `catch`, which increments `retryCount` without persisting `referenceId`. Because the earlier `findMany` selects reminders with `referenceId: null`, the next run will treat the reminder as unscheduled and schedule another SMS, creating duplicates (now additionally counting it as a retry).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:40 — Reminders that hit the retry limit are hard-deleted with no logging or alerting, so failed sends drop silently after only two attempts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` and changes the initial cleanup to `deleteMany` any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` (i.e., >=2) via the new `OR` clause. Since `retryCount` is incremented on failure paths (both the `else` branch and `catch`), reminders will be hard-deleted after two failed scheduling attempts, and this deletion happens without any logging/alerting in the shown code. This is a concrete observability/operational concern introduced by the change, but not an objectively verifiable functional defect without more requirements.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31 — New retry-count deletion/increment behavior in scheduleSMSReminders ships with no tests at all for the handler.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new behavior in `scheduleSMSReminders.ts` (e.g., deleting reminders when `retryCount > 1`, selecting `retryCount`, and incrementing it on failure paths), but the PR does not include any corresponding test additions/changes in the diff. The claim that there are “no tests at all for the handler” can’t be fully verified from the diff alone, but it is verifiable that this change ships without adding/updating tests alongside the new retry/delete logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:36 — No test asserts the retryCount>1 delete branch is scoped to SMS, so the unscoped OR that deletes EMAIL/WhatsApp reminders goes undetected.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` filter was changed to an `OR` where the second branch `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. This means running this SMS-specific handler can delete non-SMS `WorkflowReminder` rows (e.g., EMAIL/WhatsApp) that have `retryCount > 1`, which is unintended data loss and a real behavioral defect visible directly in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178 — No test covers the falsy scheduleSMS result path incrementing retryCount.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `else` branch and a `catch` block that increment `retryCount`, but it does not show any test changes or the existing test suite. From the diff alone, we cannot verify the claim that “no test covers the falsy scheduleSMS result path” because tests could exist elsewhere without being modified in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:189 — No test covers the catch path incrementing retryCount, nor what happens if that update itself throws.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial behavior: in the error path it increments `retryCount` via `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` inside the `catch` (and also in the `else` when scheduling fails). That new branch has no additional guarding—if the update in the `catch` throws, it will escape the handler since there’s no nested try/catch. While the diff doesn’t show tests, the concern is specifically about this newly added catch-path logic and its failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39 — Deletion threshold boundary (retryCount 1 vs 2, i.e. gt vs gte) is untested, so the effective max-attempts count is unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces retry-based deletion logic (`deleteMany` now deletes reminders where `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) and increments `retryCount` on failures. This makes the effective max-attempts behavior depend on the `gt` vs `gte` boundary (e.g., allowing up to 2 failed attempts before deletion vs only 1). The PR diff shows no accompanying tests or assertions verifying that intended threshold, so the finding is a specific, diff-grounded missing-verification concern rather than a demonstrable defect.
